moh rx: the message is read signed
why: Every use of `w` either compares it for equality with a constant below 0x100 or masks it with 0xf0 or 0xf, so only bits 0..7 ever matter and sign extension changes nothing but bits 16..31.  The one place the whole value is printed reads `bits[0]` again with an explicit zero extension rather than using `w`, which is what the object does at 0x8bb0 -- so that site is not covered by this mutation either; `the illegal message is printed signed` is.

label: moh rx: the illegal arm prints one rule, not two
moh rx: the illegal message is printed signed
moh rx: the illegal message prints the masked value
moh rx: MHcda and MHfrr arms are ordered before the masked ones
why: 0xbb is matched by no earlier arm -- 0xbb & 0xf0 is 0xb0, which is neither 0x50 nor 0x90, and it equals none of 0x33, 0x77 or 0x75 -- so hoisting it above them cannot change which arm any value takes.  It is here because the ORDER of the seven tests is otherwise unobservable, and this says which part of it is: the masked arms must stay ahead of nothing in particular, but 0x0150 reaching MHack depends on no exact arm matching it first.
